atoms.statement: Exploration Crew rules and Badge system must apply consistently across Ready, Hide, and Snap.
Cross-app visibility does not transfer semantic ownership.
One event may have many valid interpreters, but semantic owners do not directly mutate each other's state.
OWNER TYPE COLLAPSE: semantic owner, runtime/state owner, mutation authority, implementation owner and UI host are conflated under the word owner.
CANONICAL GENERATION DRIFT: legacy GUIDE/MAIN/Ready-centered language coexists with Learning Identity/Learning Engine/Planner/Family model.
SHADOW CURRENT STATE / PROJECTION copies current meaning across STATE, active profiles and volatile registries.
OPERATIONAL EXPRESSION PROLIFERATION and GOVERNANCE ACTIVATION GAP are stronger causes of TAKY heaviness than raw rule count.
Incident-specific app bugs are not proven to be broadly promoted into global TAKY rules; direct incident-to-global-rule leakage is weaker than initially hypothesized.
C2S is necessary complexity; it is not the primary bloat root cause unless it absorbs execution truth or creates shadow canonicals.
Learning Engine interprets; Planner manages; execution apps execute.
Ready is execution/base-camp and current runtime coordinator/UI host, not Planner or Learning Engine semantic owner.
Learning App Family owns cross-app session/handoff/routing semantics.
Exploration Crew should be modeled as a first-class logical semantic domain with Snap as current steward/incubator and canonical host, not as duplicated per-app Guide systems.
Snap stewardship does not mean permanent equivalence between Snap app lifecycle and Exploration Crew domain authority.
Shared crew identity, Visual ID lineage, core personality, name history, relationship/affinity semantics and encounter semantics remain stable across apps; only contextual behavior varies.
Ready rebuild still retains local Guide identity/name/voice system and lacks closed crew projection in specialist handoff.
OS/GUIDE_CHARACTER_RELATIONSHIP should retain family-wide relationship constraints but stop owning actual crew roster/personality/name history/affinity/encounter semantics.
SPECIAL FRIEND, READY RANDOM GUEST and SNAP SPECIAL CREW remain distinct until direct evidence proves equivalence.
Badge should be modeled as a first-class cross-app Badge Experience Domain rather than merely a Snap-local reward.
Apps emit factual/explicit experience events; apps do not directly award badges or mutate Badge History.
Badge star is tier/grade presentation and is distinct from Gem, Wish, EXP, character power and leaderboard semantics.
Ready and Hide shared badge-event producers are not yet connected; cross-app Badge History/display consistency is not closed.
Generic count-to-tier progression must not be promoted as universal badge policy; event count does not directly equal star/tier.
Historical ~60 badge names/triggers remain WORKING_DRAFT_NOT_ACTIVE; exact active catalog, thresholds and tier applicability remain open.
Ready share card generic done*5 '획득 별' conflicts with Badge star semantics and is a strong supersede/update candidate.
Learning History, Badge History, Crew Relationship Memory and Wish Economy Ledger remain separate owner histories; do not create a mega global history ledger.
Stable learner/profile identity is a shared reference key, not the semantic owner of Badge or Crew.
Profile Character Visual ID and Exploration Crew Visual ID should be separated logically; exact permanent ownership detail remains open.
Share is a composition/presentation surface and must consume projections; it must not infer or award semantic meaning.
Snap Product Growth/EXP, Snap Wish Economy, Badge Experience, Crew Affinity/World State and Learning History are distinct semantic domains even if rendered near each other.
TAKY depth should be preserved while the active surface carried into each task is reduced: DEEP MEMORY — LIGHT EXECUTION.
Semantic node does not require a new file/repository/registry; logical separation precedes physical extraction.
ENFORCEMENT_PROTOCOL is a strong candidate to be treated as mechanical/executable support rather than an independent semantic owner.
CONVERSATION_CONTEXT_LEDGER_PROTOCOL is a strong consolidation candidate because C2S/Continuity/Recovery/Traceability now own much of its former meaning.
REVISION_GOVERNANCE is a consolidation candidate into MASTER_LOGIC with compatibility pointer retained.
Persistent ACTIVE_RULE_PROFILE is a shadow-current candidate; prefer on-demand task-relevant rule composition if no indispensable consumer requires persistent projection.
STATE.md current/history contamination should be redesigned toward small current state plus historical pointers.
taky-enforcement.yml is one 59-step job spanning core, C2S/continuity, Work/Notion/Drive, executor/Codex and multiple replay families.
The problem is too-wide validation activation, not validator count alone.
Candidate CI direction: always-run aggregator + FAST CORE + affected semantic/deep suites + release/migration suites + conditional historical replay.
Validators/tests are consumers in the impact graph and can become stale when semantic/UI contracts change.
Existing BETA docs remain consulting inputs/HOLD rather than frozen execution standard because UI/C2S/Data/App streams are still converging in parallel.
Impact reopening should be targeted: NEW EVIDENCE -> OWNER -> CONTRACT -> CONSUMER -> VALIDATOR CONSUMER -> TARGETED REGRESSION.
Do not code/cleanup/dispatch Codex/merge/deploy until BETA standards freeze after sufficient convergence.
